## # CCQ — The Capability-Claim Queue (canonical state-machine reference)

SPINE LINK: this is the DEFAULT distributed-first implementation that sits BELOW the conduit
line (facet D4 of the architecture entry). It DEPENDS on the spine (shell-first, constants-
first, observability); the spine does NOT depend on it. It is swappable (Temporal-shaped) —
the conduit/CVP contracts above the line survive a swap; only what is below changes.
Canonical SSOT: docs/CCQ.md — if this entry and the code disagree, the CODE wins.

C1 — step_hash IS the status. A work item is ONE document in axon_queue; there is NO separate
status field. step_hash carries the state (*_pending = waiting / *_processing = claimed /
*_done / *_failed / terminal). metadata carries the lease: dist_processor_id (lock owner,
empty/absent = claimable), claimed_count (monotonic fencing epoch, $inc on every reclaim),
started_at (read ONLY by stale-recovery), retry_after / retry_count. payload = opaque,
product-shaped input; result = worker output. Rows are INDEPENDENT — a flat, unordered POOL,
not FIFO, NEVER referencing another row. A multi-step pipeline is ONE row whose step_hash
mutates in place, claimed by a different-capability poller at each step — NEVER a chain of
linked rows.

C2 — Claim MUST be a globally-atomic CAS. One findOneAndUpdate, NEVER read-then-write
(filter: step_hash==watchStep AND dist_processor_id empty/absent AND retry_after
absent/null/<=now; update: $set step_hash=claimStep, owner, started_at + $inc claimed_count).
Correctness comes from this ONE primitive — NO external coordinator (no Temporal server, no
Redis lock); the DB picks the single winner of every claim. Route by step_hash ALONE
(capability is already proven at poller creation; workspace_id is traceability, not a gate).

C3 — Commit MUST be epoch-fenced (the §65 INVARIANT). EVERY result-write / step-advance MUST
be a CAS on the claim epoch (filter: _id==id AND claimed_count==epoch). NEVER a blind
UpdateOne({_id}). No match => FENCED: a stale-reclaimed, slow-but-alive worker's late write is
REJECTED (not an error — a lost race) and a ccq_fenced_write telemetry row is emitted (id,
epoch, owner, step). dist_processor_id alone is an INSUFFICIENT fence (a same-node reclaim
keeps it); claimed_count is the monotonic Kleppmann token that makes exclusion total.

C4 — Recovery is the release half + a budget. A sweep every StaleRecoveryInterval (1m): an
item stuck *_processing with started_at < now-OrphanAfter (5m) is RESET to *_pending (clear
owner) if claimed_count < StaleReclaimLimit (3), else QUARANTINED at StepStaleExhausted. The
reset does NOT bump the epoch; the NEXT claim does — so claimed_count = the number of times
the item was assigned = the fence value. Quarantine stops two perpetually-slow workers
alternating reclaim -> fenced -> reclaim forever.

C5 — Honest guarantee: exactly-once EFFECT on persisted state, at-least-once EXECUTION. A
globally-atomic claim excludes other claimers only at the INSTANT of claiming, NOT for the
work's duration; the DB cannot tell "dead" from "slow". Safety therefore lives on the COMMIT
(the epoch fence), NOT the claim. A fenced worker's external (claude) call STILL RAN and was
billed — only its output is thrown away. NEVER claim "exactly-once execution"; deduping
execution needs an idempotency key on the external call [future].

C6 — Chat is the deliberately-SIMPLE flow (NOT decomposed). ChatService.Chat writes
conversation + user ply + a PENDING assistant ply directly, enqueues ONE step_llm_call_pending,
and returns. The worker runs claude --resume and advances to done; Thread->resolvePending
reconciles the answer on READ. Grounding is synchronous + best-effort. Chat does NOT flow into
SSOT/embed (that tail is the unbuilt F9 path). SSOT INVARIANT: Mongo is authoritative; qdrant
is a DERIVED index; every point carries a mongo_id back-reference; nothing lands in embedded
storage except as the output of Mongo-write -> embed -> upsert.

PURITY (why CCQ is a pure joint): the machine is DOMAIN-BLIND — step_hash / claim / fence /
budget are pure coordination, ZERO domain meaning. Chat, synth, embed, search, RAG, A2A all
ride through as opaque payload; the SAME machine serves all because it knows none of them.
Provenance (client_id, §60) rides metadata, NEVER the step_hash.

## CVP — Continuous Verification Probe (Agentic Lifecycle)

SPINE LINK: CVP is the post-deploy, DIVERSE-REDUNDANT second lens (a different lens from CI) that
ORCHESTRATES the live probes (LCP/LPP — see the Conduit/Orchestrator entry) across axon's WHOLE
temporal axis. It is the MANAGEMENT arm for the un-weldable joints (doc/code drift, portal<->worker
partition, worker liveness) — making them DETECTABLE, not preventable. CVP itself is a CCQ SAGA
(constants/cvp.go): its OWN collection cvp_queue, the SAME poller molecules (claim / fence /
stale_recovery); lifecycle rides step_hash (step_cvp_pending -> claimed -> done); the PHASE rides
the payload (cvp_phase: setup -> exercise -> teardown -> done) = the idempotent RESUME cursor;
cvp_mutations = the compensation blob; verdict pass/fail. CVP verifies the conduit BY RIDING it.

PHASES 0->3 (run IN ORDER; STOP at the first failed gate). P0 LOUD red-flag GATE — 0a epistemic
(stale / contradicting / outdated distill across the temporal axis -> STOP + emit re distill /
blast radius / discovery distill / horizon distill); 0b mechanical (enumerate the teardown surface
+ a unique WORKSPACE seal + collision-check count==0 or ABORT). P1 filesystem/RAM conduit probe ->
VCS golden (regression + the teardown ground truth). P2 ./dev.sh OPERATIONAL RUN (see AGENTIC
LIFECYCLE). P3 invasive live, TWO lenses: 3A platform/RAG conduit (qa_with_remote_db canary under
the seal), 3B base learning product (qa). TEARDOWN: DeleteMany({workspace_id: seal}) + assert the
footprint re-queries to 0; never leave the seal's data behind.

AGENTIC ./dev.sh LIFECYCLE (P2 — the agent DRIVES this; it is REAL CVP work, not narration):
- RUN/RESTART ONLY via ./dev.sh — NEVER a bare binary / go run for the SERVER or WORKER; dev.sh
  holds the validations + guardrails. The agent owns on/off: worker OFF during source edits, ON
  (rebuilds via ./dev.sh) before live verification, OFF after. ANNOUNCE before toggling on the
  developer's machine.
- KILL-BY-PORT to free a stale instance before restart (dev.sh does this with
  'lsof -ti :PORT | kill -9'; the agent may too). The TWO dev.sh-managed backend ports are $PORT
  (portal, default 3456) and $_AC_PORT (axon_core poller, default 3461). Frontend is Vite, built
  per product.
- PEEK CONFIG given a PASSED env var, WITHOUT starting the server, via the dry-run tools (verified):
  'go run ./cmd/config-explain -mode masked' prints the resolved snapshot with PROVENANCE — a
  passed PERSISTENT_LAYER / MONGO_URI shows as last_delegator=env; 'go run . validate'
  (= './axon validate', the Fly gateway's own validator) FATALS on a bad env (PERSISTENT_LAYER=banana
  -> "must be one of {file, mongodb}" + a fix-hint, exit 1). READ-ONLY: no port, no server, no toggle.
- WORKER UP/DOWN MATRIX (the local worker is a CVP VARIABLE): negative = worker DOWN -> the job sits
  step_llm_call_pending UNCLAIMED; positive = worker UP (./dev.sh) -> advances pending -> processing
  -> done. VERIFY in axon_db, NOT the HTTP body. Machine-detect — do NOT fake the positive row on a
  non-worker box.

LIVE TOPOLOGY. Fly = the worker-less §57 gateway (CMD ./axon -> startup.Validate at boot, with
prod-only rules); the LOCAL ./dev.sh instance is the worker/poller. CVP exercises BOTH surfaces
(deploy to Fly + run dev.sh locally). The §66 affinity lock (INSTANCE_LOCK_ID / metadata.locked_to)
is the fix where CVP and the live worker race on step_hash.

## Cheap Checks — Run the Deterministic Gate After Every 'Done' Task / Pre-Commit

DETERMINISTIC GATE (cheap checks + heuristics). UNCONDITIONAL TRIGGER: run this AFTER a unit is
"done" (a package · a feature wired end-to-end · a doc/qa artifact) and BEFORE every commit — it is
also wired as the git pre-commit hook. One command:
  bash scripts/distill_checks.sh              # FAST: grep + .sh, NO Go builds (the pre/post-distill gate)
  bash scripts/distill_checks.sh --hard-only  # blocking subset only (the fast pre-commit path)
  bash scripts/distill_checks.sh --full       # adds build-heavy boot-fatal / import-graph / ticket-lineage
Exit 0 = all HARD checks pass; 1 = a HARD check failed. WARN checks print but NEVER change the exit code.

PHILOSOPHY — cheap by construction:
- grep + bash, NEVER static analysis / tree-sitter / AST. Milliseconds, no build dependency, one-screen
  auditable.
- A grep over source text false-positives (it greps strings, not import-scopes) → flag it WARN (prints,
  advises, never blocks). Only currently-green, trustworthy checks are HARD (block the commit).
- RATCHET: promote a WARN to HARD once its legacy debt clears or the check tightens to import-scope.
- Recall over precision: catch the CLASS of mistake the moment it lands, on every cycle.

TOP HIGH-RECALL PICKS (reach for these first; each catches a class nothing else does):
1. check_tsc.sh (tsc --noEmit) — broadest; ANY .ts(x) edit. Catches type/import/prop drift + FE-BE
   symbol mismatch instantly. The cheapest, most inseparable probe — edited TypeScript ⇒ run it.
2. probe_clauding_mistarget.sh — the agent-specific WRONG-PLACE write: code landing OUTSIDE workspace.yml
   clauding_targets (a different product / a sealed internal). Pure git-diff × path grep. Otherwise
   INVISIBLE until much later (the foundry-in-the-wrong-product failure).
3. check_bson_parity.sh — SILENT data loss: a missing bson: tag lowercases the field name → missing data
   at runtime with NO panic / NO error. The only cheap guard for a class that emits zero runtime signal.
Honourable mention: check_triplet_coverage.sh — the (product_name, producer, step_hash) triplet keeps
queue/telemetry rows greppable and filterable in axon_db.

THE BLAST-RADIUS GREP (a reflex, not a script) — before introducing OR relying on any domain string:
  grep -rn '"<raw_value>"' --include="*.go"   # every hit outside constants/ is a greppability violation

The check_*.sh family is the SSOT; distill_checks.sh orchestrates them and documents the HARD/WARN split
+ each ratchet target in its own header. The qa/* substrate these run within (build tags, the init.go
bridge, the check_qa_isolation isolation rule, the ONEOFF marker) lives in the on-demand
Local-Workspace-Quirks cluster — reach THERE to author or modify a check; reach HERE to run the gate.

## Verification Ladder — Probe Cheap-First (tsc → heuristics → build → deploy → CVP)

VERIFICATION LADDER — a change is verified by a LADDER of probes, CHEAPEST rung first. You climb only after the rung below is GREEN, and each rung catches a class the cheaper rungs CANNOT.

SPINE LINK: this is the PRE-deploy complement to CVP + UI-CVP, which are the TOP rung (post-deploy, real browser, U1-U5). Those directives assume the artifact already compiles + builds; THIS one names the rungs below them and forbids inverting the order.

V1 — THE LADDER (cheapest → costliest; the ONLY valid order):
  1. tsc --noEmit (~1s) — does it COMPILE? HARD gate in distill_checks (check_tsc.sh). Use `tsc -b`      (build mode follows references): the shell/product tsconfigs are SOLUTION files (references-only),      so bare `tsc --noEmit` checks NOTHING and passes trivially. Inseparable from any .ts edit;      NON-NEGOTIABLE after a lossy copy.
  2. grep heuristics (check_*.sh via distill_checks) — is it CONFORMANT? (parity, fe-be pairs, no raw      fetch, tokens-only, FSD).
  3. local build — does the BUNDLE build + NAME correctly? (VITE_PRODUCT_NAME ← server/constants.go      ProductName; missing ⇒ '.js' empty-name bundle ⇒ 404).
  4. deploy — does it SHIP in the image?
  5. CVP (real browser, U1-U5) — does it RENDER + behave for a real user?

V2 — DEPLOY/CVP IS THE LAST RUNG, NEVER THE FIRST. Reaching a costlier rung before a cheaper one is the inversion that lets a 1-second-catchable error (a TS syntax error in registry.ts) cost a multi-minute Fly build. deploy-fly-io.sh runs distill_checks (now tsc-gated) BEFORE `fly deploy` for exactly this reason. If a cheap rung exists and you skipped it, you inverted the ladder.

V3 — THE TOP RUNG IS NOT OPTIONAL: some classes ONLY surface there. tsc proves a thing COMPILES, never that it is CORRECT. A semantically-valid-but-wrong string — an HTTP header name with SPACES, 'X-UI HR Playground-Client-Id' — passes tsc + grep + build + deploy and breaks auth ONLY in a live browser (fetch() throws on the invalid name → getAuthIdentity throws → roles=[] → empty nav, while /api/auth/state itself still returns 200). A lossy copy MUST climb all the way to CVP.

V4 — CLONE = LOSSY COPY (the canonical ladder exercise). clone-product.sh string-swaps + inserts, so it can: corrupt PLATFORM constants (a global s/Axon/<name>/g rewrote X-Axon-Build / X-Axon-Client-Id — the swap is now guarded against collision-prone tokens); DROP identity (no server/constants.go ⇒ empty ProductName ⇒ '.js' bundle ⇒ 404); MIS-INSERT (registry.ts '^}' also matched the ProductProps interface ⇒ invalid TS — now anchored on '^};'); MIS-SCOPE visibility (roles=[admin,<id>] is invisible to every magic-link/demo session, and Fly has no admin login). Each is a different rung's catch. The full ladder IS the clone's acceptance test — a REGISTERED product is not a VERIFIED one.

V5 — GATES CHECK PRESENCE, NOT VALIDITY (know the blind spot). product-registry-parity greps the KEY, not TS validity — a malformed registry.ts PASSES parity yet FAILS tsc. So tsc sits ALONGSIDE the parity greps, not behind them. When a deterministic gate is presence-only, the validity rung (tsc/CVP) is mandatory, not redundant.
